Root reads this as Theo's answer to the lsshells/m3-plan.md 'Theo decides' items: (1) near-Go growth, including effect long, is worth M3 D3; (2) the PORTING.md AST contract change for language server file versions (accessors stop being &'static for freeable versions; 'a published file is never freed' ends for them) is approved as the route to that fix, with the independent reviewer checking it at each revision; (3) freeable rule: the safe option (language server or API process, path published before); (4) M3e text after M3d is measured. Order change: M2a, M2b and M3a to M3d start now on main (pin 52168999f3dc, branch goport-lsshells) instead of after bump B. Bump B wave 3 merges main again after each accepted memory revision. Each memory revision goes through the normal candidate pipeline with both verdicts. R131 = crate split step 1 (ready, small overlap); memory revisions follow.

value.decision: Theo 2026-09-28: 'should we be deprecating the old stuff and removing it? this project is greenfield, we can delete whatever'. Root answer: yes. Facts: no roster crate depends on ts_goport, but ts_goport depends on 12 legacy crates, including ts_compiler, which pulls in ts_checker (1.32M lines), ts_binder and ts_printer. Plan: workflow legacy-removal-audit (read only) maps each use and the acceptance pipeline, then staged removal: cut goport's legacy dependencies; retire the legacy cargo roster (the 6,055 and 6,330 names test the old stack) and make goport's own tests and gate items the protected baseline; delete the legacy crates and tools. The acceptance-rule change is made under this message from Theo and is recorded in acceptanceRuleChanges when it lands. Historical evidence stays unchanged. R131 finishes under the current rules.

Theo 2026-09-28, direct approval: 'i approve any rule changes that allow removing the legacy code'. This approves the acceptance-rule changes needed to retire the legacy cargo roster (ts_checker, ts_compiler, ts_fixture stages, the current-source corpus, the 6,055 and 6,330 legacy names) and to delete the legacy crates, tools and scripts. Root will write the replacement rule (goport's own tests per name and the gate items become the protected set; no lost pass allowed) into docs/typechecker-accountability.md and AGENTS.md and record it in acceptanceRuleChanges citing this approval. acceptanceRuleChanges.scope: Every batch opened after R132 (open_revision.py --new-batch sets protectedSet goport). The protected set is goport's own evidence: every goport test name (docs/goport-protected/tests-r131.json.gz, then the results of the last accepted goport revision), every gate item against the last accepted gate manifest, every gate run of the source (gateRuns; a failed run needs a flake note for each regression), the bound Query and Hono runs, the LSP oracle (6 batteries) and API oracle (10 batteries) per request, np-suite, quality and both verdicts. After a legacy batch the test, API and np-suite bases are the R131 runs (tests-r131.json.gz, api-r131, np-r131). While the defect editor-long-growth is open, editor/query-core/long and editor/hono/long can FAIL only on growth, at most the fixed caps in gate-compare.py LONG_CAP (query-core 1.58, hono 1.28 MiB/edit). A cap only goes down; only Theo can raise one. A lost, absent or unrun base pass is STOP; new passes do not compensate. Name maps only for pin bumps and moved or replaced tests, with Go evidence at the new pin, checked by the reviewer. The legacy cargo roster (6,055 and 6,330 names), the roster drive, the current-source corpus and the roster carry-forward are retired for new batches; R132 (batch port-18, opened under them before this rule) is the last revision under them. For goport batches this replaces the 'Protected cargo roster' clause of pin-bump-batch. Old batches keep their rules. Root must not widen it. Gate tools: every tool hash in the gate manifest (oracle, Go dumper, gate.sh, allow list, stage scripts, saved Go output families in oracleCaches) must equal the base run's, unless batch.gateToolChanges lists the exact change for the reviewer. Evidence builds: only the candidate checkout builds in the shared candidate target.

value.hypothesis: No goport output uses the legacy loader or the legacy crate stack. Deleting them keeps goport and tsgo stdout, exit codes and emitted files byte-equal to R132, keeps every protected goport test name, takes the None-arm checks out of the hot paths, and makes a clean release build about 2.7x faster (208 s to 76 s on dbook-lan).
value.change: R132 + goport-legacy2 3a94ce888. Stage 2: remove the GOPORT_FRONTEND=legacy loader and every legacy fallback in program.rs, options.rs, core.rs, ast/*, go_frontend.rs, execute/tsc/diagnostics.rs and modulespecifiers/host.rs; delete ast/jsdoc.rs, ast/parser_flags.rs, ast/go_view.rs and program/verify_options.rs; keep the 2 alias resolver arms; goport no longer depends on ts_compiler, ts_parser, ts_diagnostic_writer, ts_module, ts_options or ts_vfs; lib blobs regenerated. Stage 3: delete the 23 legacy crates (keep crates/ts_bundled/libs/), tools/ts_fixture, tools/ts_compare, the legacy scripts, docs and dead test data. Workspace: ts_goport, goport_util, goport_lsproto, the 6 kept crates (ts_ast, ts_core, ts_diagnostics, ts_jsnum, ts_path, ts_scanner) and the 2 codegen tools.

value.hypothesis: When a run gets 4 KiB pages (fragmented memory, THP off or never), a worker copy of tsgo does the work and sends its exit code over a pipe once its output is written, so tsgo exits without waiting about 50 ms for its memory to unmap. Effect emit on fragmented memory gets 54 to 56 ms faster (32 CPUs 1.79x to 1.92x, 16 CPUs 1.86x to 1.99x of Go). Runs on clean memory keep the R136 path. Every output stays byte-equal, and the exit code or death signal a caller sees is the same as without a worker.
value.change: R136 + goport-perf16 23c474d4d: thp_guard returns whether the run gets huge pages; bin/tsgo.rs launch starts a worker copy when it does not (GOPORT_LAUNCH=0 off, 1 on; not for --lsp, --api or watch). The worker sets a parent-death SIGKILL, checks getppid against GOPORT_LAUNCHER_PID, points stdout and stderr at /dev/null and writes its exit code to the pipe at exit. The launcher sends SIGINT and SIGTERM on to the worker and, when the worker dies by a signal, dies by the same signal (signal-hook emulate_default_handler). rustix gets the stdio feature. build-release.sh and build-pgo.sh export GOPORT_LAUNCH=0 for the training runs.

value.hypothesis: Five gap audit fixes and the R137 worker hardening close gaps with Go, and emit and check output on query, hono, zod and effect stays byte-equal to R137. (1) pjcache: multi-threaded -p --incremental writes Go's packageJsons and missingPackageJsons lists, the same in each run. (2) sortfix: each ported Go sort site uses the Go sort that it ports, so a comparator that is not a total order (compareSymbols) cannot panic, and the vscode imports codeAction and completion panics stop. (3) stacks: thread stacks and glibc arenas follow RLIMIT_AS and RLIMIT_DATA, so query check and emit give Go's output under ulimit -v 2G to 8G, where R137 exits 70; with no limit nothing changes. (4) identity: a build-time version and a port of Go's noembed build let a release build match shipped tsc 7.0.2, and the default build is unchanged. (5) platforms1: cfg gates let ts_goport pass cargo check for darwin, windows and arm64 Linux, and fswatch uses the target's open flags on arm64 Linux. (6) R137 follow-up 3: a tsgo is a worker only when its parent is the launcher, so a tsgo started from a worker runs as a plain tsgo and is not killed. R137 follow-up 2: the tsgo CLI audit gives the same results at GOPORT_LAUNCH=1, GOPORT_LAUNCH=0 and Go.
value.change: main 3717d4d9a (R137) + goport-gaps1-int d14ba56e3: merges of goport-pjcache 2025dbc7b, goport-sortfix 5a4b95150, goport-stacks 8ea06f135, goport-identity 9005711bd and goport-platforms1 40a17f2e3, then 3 commits. pjcache: each SharedResolutionCache answer carries the package.json lookups of its resolution (SharedResolution, PackageJsonLookup), and Resolver::package_json_cache_entries adds the lookups of the answers that the loader took (incremental and -b runs only). sortfix: 36 std sort calls and 1 hand-written insertion sort change to gostd::slices sorts (21 sort_func, 6 sort_slice, 10 sort_stable_func), each with its Go reference; sorts of plain ordered values and port-only sorts on Ord keys stay on std; PORTING.md says never to use a std sort with a comparator; 2 gostd::slices unit tests. stacks: new gostd::stack::max_stack_size (1 GiB with no limit, else 1/64 of the smaller of RLIMIT_AS and RLIMIT_DATA, clamped to 8 MiB..1 GiB, from rustix getrlimit, computed once) at all 19 stack sites; ThreadBudget::glibc_tunables gives arena_max=1 under an address space or data limit, and set_malloc_tunables sets only the variables that the caller did not set and execs only when one is left; 1 unit test. identity: core.rs VERSION reads option_env!(GOPORT_BUILD_VERSION), default 7.1.0-dev, and modulespecifiers uses it; Go embed.go moves to frontend/bundled/embed.rs and the new noembed.rs ports noembed.go behind cargo feature noembed; the parse snapshot key hashes the lib base name; build-release.sh adds noembed when RELEASE_VERSION is set; new scripts/copy-libs.sh. platforms1: nix and name-to-handle-at become Linux-only dependencies and jemalloc is not built for msvc; fswatch unix.rs and walkdir_unix.rs are Linux only, Errno moves to fswatch/syscall.rs, and the O_* and IN_* flags come from rustix for the target with compile-time checks against the Go amd64 and arm64 values; realpath uses canonicalize off Linux (Go realpath_other.go); unix-only std calls are behind cfg(unix). a83b66339 (R137 follow-up 3): worker() accepts GOPORT_WORKER_FD only when getppid() equals GOPORT_LAUNCHER_PID, decided once at the start of main, and launch, end_with_launcher and exit use it; the launcher makes the pipe close-on-exec and clears the flag only on the write end, so the worker no longer gets the read end (its write end stays inherited, because no safe call sets the flag on an fd number); new test tests/tsgo_launch.rs. 851ca312c: the LIMIT_SHARE comment gives the measured --checkers 48 exit 70 at ulimit -v 1G. d14ba56e3: lib_parse.bin regenerated after the merges (stored keys only); lib_bind.bin unchanged.

Unknown real-path keys (hard-linked build info, .. in a link target) also give build order and turn off the prefetch. Imports that leave rootDir (TS6059) keep completion order: a config-only check cannot see them; both values are in Go set.

apisess1 decisions and known limits (R151 reviewer item 4): R14: the --async API handles requests one at a time in order; Go N handles each in its own goroutine, so pipelined dependent requests can differ (Go itself fails them with snapshot not found in 10 of 10 runs). Kept serial: a concurrent session needs thread-safe session state; revisit only with a design. Known limits, same as R149 or Go: a client callback with no answer blocks LSP shutdown (followups1 works on it), one extra stderr line at stdin EOF while a callback waits, a second API session blocks the first. No protected test pins the L11 fix yet.

R151 reviewer item 6: open_revision.py reset the batch auditor and reviewer ids to pending on every revision, also a later revision in the same batch. Now it keeps the batch ids there and resets only the verdict; a new batch still starts with pending ids. Protected tool change for the next reviewer to judge.

lspfix1 skeptic: f82723ec5 (D1b and A1, run the pending warm before a no-change snapshot) reverses the race: Go runs the warm on a background goroutine and with any real dependency the next request wins and Go discards the warm, which is what R156 does (hono: Go no fix 7/7, R156 same; new offers a fix every run; first implementation after an edit 49 ms vs Go 15 on query-core). Root decision: revert f82723ec5 and its test at integration; record D1b and A1 in the D1 auto-import warm race class (editfuzz2 option c), superseding the D1b part of editfuzz2-decisions-2026-10-02. Take the other three lspfix1 commits (P2-1 crash fix, P1 Go panic text, R1 insertion order). followups9 skeptic: item 4 (go_signal_handlers before set_malloc_tunables, which can exec) loses signals (3 to 6 per 1000 quiet, up to 14% under load): round b.

tscbpar1 round f skeptic FAIL (tscbpar1/f/wf-result.txt): two new finish-order blockers (b41d9070d root-count rule, 2e81049f5 lowest-index rule) give answers that differ from Go N and R155 in 44 attack cells where Go and R155 agree; the no-builder timing rule still fails. Per tscbpar1-round-f-decision-2026-10-02: the current builder design (goport-tscbpar1, rounds a to f) is not taken; its gains (hono-b noop -18% to -25%, wide -11% to -36%, mixlib5s -21%) are recorded as not taken. Cause: the port holds builder writes in memory and the orchestrator chooses the finish order; in Go each routine writes its own outputs when its task ends and only the reports are ordered (orchestrator.go:891-904 rangeTasks). A possible new design (not started): the exact Go model, where each slot builds and writes its own task and the reporter waits per task in Order(); output order then depends on timing as in Go. The build-wide parse cache (round d, Go parseCache.go) can be reused there. Not queued until other lanes finish.

resolveahead1 (goport-resolveahead1 e8fea0f02, skeptic PASS candidateReady): LSP p95 query-core 21.5/21.9 vs Go 24.6/25.2 ms; effect 25.6/26.1 vs Go 26.0/26.2 (under or equal); effect import add still 0.7 to 0.9 ms over Go median; costs: session CPU +5% to +11% (0.38 to 0.66 of Go), the edit after a load 0.04 to 0.4 ms slower. Root decision: round 2 on the same branch (plan step 1b trims, persistent worker pool, free off the dispatch thread) before integration; take round 2 if its skeptic passes, else take round 1 as is.

tscbgo1 study and critic (studies/tscbgo1/summary.md, critic.md): Go N tsc -b output depends on timing when one task reads another task output without a reference (F1 read vs write, F2 slot take, F3 end order); Go is stable at default settings in most F1 and F2 cells, the current serial R157 differs from Go default in 7 light F2 cells and in ew900, em1800, fd60 to fd110 type shapes. The exact Go model (each slot writes its own outputs, reports in Order) is the only design that can follow Go, but a lane needs an output rule for racy shapes (an answer-set rule), which is an acceptance rule change and needs Theo. lspwait1 (wf_1d1917a2-1b8, lspwait1/wf-result.txt) skeptic FAIL on a605eff6d. Decision: DROP the lane (both parts), no merge. (1) cancel1 moves away from Go: Go dispatches each request at once, so a cancel usually finds it running and Go answers a result (hover, documentSymbol, references, workspace/symbol, rename 3 of 3); R169 also answers a result; the lane answers -32800 for every kind. R169 already gives Go common answer: keep it. (2) The serving wait (slow registerCapability reply) gives 50 to 70 ms for queued messages at one level but nested tasks get slower than R169 (up to 3.1 s) and one case leaves 2 watch registrations that Go and R169 remove (an inner task unwatch runs before the outer task records the id). It helps only clients that reply to registerCapability after 50 ms (VS Code replies in under 1 ms). Recorded as known differences of the single dispatch thread: a queued request waits for a snapshot task client reply (R169: up to the 1 s watch timeout per call; Go answers at once); cancelled queued requests answer with their result after the slow request (Go: result, sooner). Revisit only with a design that runs snapshot tasks off the dispatch thread without reentrancy.

getsym1 (read-only, getsym1/report.md): measured the same way on both sides (mini-743d, single-threaded, perf cycles and instructions, equal call counts), GetSymbolAtLocation is 1.26x Go cycles (1,174 vs 929) and 1.97x instructions; effperf0's 1.7x used pprof time for Go and was wrong. Name resolution is not the cause (resolveEntityName port 552 vs Go 591 cycles). The gap is the node read path: every kind(), parent() or name() reads FILE_BLOCKS[file], a OnceLock acquire load, a column pointer and a bounds check (10 to 20 instructions where Go reads one field), and the acquire load stops the compiler from merging repeated reads (is_in_right_side_of_import_or_export_assignment 171 vs 17 instructions). AST walk: 60 vs 27 cycles per entry; leaf nodes cost about 68 instructions (Go 13); each child id goes through an out-of-line req or opt call (25 vs 7). Fix designs, output-equal, Go model: W1 leaf early return, W2 inline child handles, W3 astdump hook out of the hot walk, G1 NodeRef view (one registry lookup per predicate), G2 the same view at the top lookup sites (flow, Node::name, binder; at least -1.0 percent instructions on plain effect), G4 resolveEntityName with &Name. intern1 (read-only, intern1/report.md): intern::text costs 0.44 to 0.87 percent of single-thread instructions (36 per call) on the gate projects; Go keeps the string and hashes it on each lookup, so id compares with the stored hash are cheaper than Go except at sort sites. Ten small fixes save 0.16 (hono) to 0.75 (zod) percent instructions; fix 5 makes Name hash bit-equal to the str hash under FxHasher from the stored 64-bit hash (no map order change; test hash_one(name) == hash_one(name.as_str())). Design: per-pool arena claims in program.rs start_checkers (about :3544, next to the singleThreaded bind): a checker keeps jemalloc's choice unless a checker of its pool holds that arena, then moves to the lowest auto arena no pool checker holds (never empties an arena); about 40 lines; tested with an LD_PRELOAD shim: 0 shares in 238 runs, pages and wall equal the no-share runs. astchunks0 (astchunks0/report.md): Go puts 90 to 96 percent of parsed nodes in typed arenas (core.Arena, 256-value chunks, header inside the data). The port makes 0.98 to 1.39 mallocs per parsed node (50 to 57 percent of nodes get a jemalloc Box of their data); node data is 60 to 64 B per node plus 50 B of slot columns (Go 84 to 86 B all in). Most of the memory gain comes from the lists (inline NodeList, PendingList, Vec copy) and unread binder fields: step 1 saves 3.1 (zod) to 7.4 (query) percent default peak RSS; the arena itself adds 0.4 to 1.0 percent; the boxes are about 2.3 percent of parse cycles. Separate finding: the JSDoc parser makes one String per comment token (24 to 30 percent of parse mallocs), Go keeps substrings: -1.8 to -2.8 percent parse cycles. effperf2 (effperf2/report.md): the Effect plugin is 1.40 to 1.45x effect-tsgo in single-thread cycles, nearly all from hash maps (Go 4.2 to 8.0 G map cycles, port 0.45 to 0.86 G); AST reads 1.6 to 2.1x Go; the checker re-checks behind GetTypeAtLocation only 1.02 to 1.14x; ten fixes about -10.5 percent effect-on cycles (item 1 one pre-order node list per file -4.5, item 2 member name keys -3.4, items 3 to 10 small); effect-on 2x single-thread needs general checker work. value.text: fastmode1 goport-fastmode1 cfaafee5a (on main 8cb5469fc, R195 source) skeptic PASS. tsgo --fast or GOPORT_FAST=1: checkers one per core (4 to 16, at most one per 32 non-declaration files; explicit --checkers or --singleThreaded wins; tsc -b keeps 4), work stealing in the first check pass, lazy members, fast never order, own jemalloc arenas past 4. Default path byte-equal to R195 (tests 0 lost, identity, counts on 8 projects, full stdout on the apps). Testbox, 16 of 32 vCPUs: 6 apps geomean default/--fast 1.70x, --fast/Bun 1.28x (was about 2.2x); VS Code 5.41 to 2.20 s (Bun 1.70), Sentry 5.63 to 2.32 s (Bun 2.84), T3 Code sum 7.56 to 6.05 s (Bun 4.81). Peak RSS up to 2.2x default. --fast output equals default on 14 of 15 projects; zod and zod-v4 cycle TS2344 and TS5115 depend on the checker count as in Go (tsc-rs equals tsgo --checkers N), and with stealing they change from run to run. Skeptic non-blocking: README wording (16 of 32 vCPUs under taskset; zod text), arenas.create arenas miss the 4 MiB alignment and watch or tsc -b pools leak up to 12 arenas each, early emit off whenever stealing is on.

Root decision (goal mode, no questions; Theo can override): --fast is deterministic. Work stealing is off by default in --fast and opt-in with GOPORT_FAST_STEAL=1, because with stealing the zod cycle diagnostics change from run to run, and a type checker in CI must give the same output on each run. Without stealing, --fast output equals tsgo --checkers N for the machine's N. Cost: VS Code 2.26 to 2.66 s and Sentry 2.30 to 2.77 s (skeptic, one run each); Excalidraw gains 0.73 to 0.65 s. Lane fastmode2 flips the default, fixes the skeptic items, and measures a deterministic cost-balanced static split to win back the stealing gain (that split equals itself on every run but not Go's split in split-dependent cases; it becomes the --fast default only if it gains 10 percent or more on VS Code and Sentry, and root reports it to Theo). Making --fast the default mode stays Theo's decision (decision C). Next big lever after fastmode lands: sharedstore0 stage 0 probe (T3 server class, est. 0.50 to 0.65x wall).

bundledpath1 goport-bundledpath1 dc8cd3c23 dropped (skeptic FAIL). Go model (citations checked): filesParser.start stores the first task to reach a path with LoadOrStore (filesparser.go:279), and getProcessedFiles counts the file as a lib only when that first task is a lib task; in default mode each task is a goroutine, so whichever route (the lib reference chain or an import through paths) arrives first wins; --singleThreaded runs the work group LIFO so the lib chain always wins (the port s order in every mode). The lane replayed the race on a fitted cost clock (settle_lib_races): it matched the lane s 41 stable cases but the skeptic found 11 of 32 new stable cases wrong, 7 of them regressions against R212 (Go keeps es5 at its lib place once the root file passes about 8 to 16 KiB of real code; the cost model charged bytes, not parse work) and misses with many roots (Go queues the lib root task after all root files, fileloader.go:207-230). Root decision: this is a Go goroutine race whose winner depends on parse times; a cost model cannot follow it; the port keeps Go s --singleThreaded order (deterministic), which equals Go default mode once the root work is large. Known class GN-LIBRACE: a file reached by both a lib reference chain and a non-lib route (paths to bundled:///libs) in Go default mode. Branch kept, not for merge.

Goal t3-dropin-2 (Theo: make tsc-rs a drop-in for the typescript package in T3 Code). Root decisions: (1) new published package @tsc-rs/typescript with bin tsc and Go's typescript package layout (lib/tsc.js, Go's lib/getExePath.js unchanged, lib/version.cjs, dist, schemas, vendor); npm version = the tsc-rs version. (2) It reuses the @tsc-rs/<os>-<arch> platform packages through alias optionalDependencies named @typescript/typescript-<os>-<arch> (npm:@tsc-rs/<os>-<arch>@<v>), because both Go's getExePath.js and the VS Code TypeScript 7 extension (packages/vscode-typescript util.ts resolveTsdkPathToExe and tsdkPackage.ts resolvePackageExecutable, same at microsoft/TypeScript main 2026-10-21) resolve @typescript/typescript-<platform>-<arch>/package.json from the main package dir and need a package name whose base is typescript with bin tsc. So an install as typescript: npm:@tsc-rs/typescript@<v> finds its binary in the CLI and in VS Code with the tsdk setting node_modules/typescript/lib. (3) tsc-rs getExePath looks up @tsc-rs/<os>-<arch> by a fixed name, not from package.json name. (4) Lanes: t3pkg1 (packaging, worktree goport-t3pkg1), t3inc1 (incremental slow path, worktree goport-t3inc1), t3effect (Effect editor parity list, read-only), t3vscode (headless VS Code check). Evidence builds: only the candidate checkout builds in the shared candidate target.

stack99 (wf_d0964f6c-0f0; oct22/stack99/measure.md, go-note.md, go-note-check.md): issue #99 on a 984 KiB Node main thread (release wasm): + and comma noEmit fail in check at L about 2192 (last pass 2126); &&, ||, ?? fail in bind at L 1622 (1573); with emit on every op fails in the ES module transform visitor at about L 1270 (1228 to 1246); parens parse 636 to 643; ?: flow walk overflows at L 1859 before the TS2563 guard. Per level: bind 360 to 617 B, check 465, transform 767, facts 440. Native: 1 GiB Go-style thread stacks, 20,000 and 100,000 terms pass (14x margin at 100k). Strada 6.0.3 on the same thread: + passes 20,000; &&, ||, ?? fail at 1,000 in bind; parens fail at 1,000. Go recurses per level in bind, check and the transforms (goroutine stacks grow to 1 GB). Design (go-note.md, checked: text fixes only): option B (binder only) gains nothing; option C (binder and checker loops, TS 5.x trampoline shape, Go visit order) fixes the issue repro (noEmit, 3,000 terms); option D (transform visitors, subtree facts, flow walk) is needed for emit; check notes M1 (isSideEffectFree on comma) and M2 (getSyntacticNullishnessSemantics on ??) recurse too; CI test at 5,000 terms (O(N^2) time at 20,000). Root decision (goal mode, recommended option): document the stack need now (npm/wasm/README.md, 1 MB host numbers), keep #99 open with the measurements, and queue option C as one lane after bump E wave 2 lands (bump E lane L3 owns src/checker/**; a checker loop now would collide), then option D if a user needs emit at that depth. Checker and binder loops move hot paths away from Go's shape, so the lane takes the full path with timing.

PR #93 + #95 audit (wf_74f94441-fef and wf_ffc2e98a-8e3; target/continuation-r97-goport/pr95audit/report.md, skeptic.md, skeptic93.md). Answer for Theo: do not merge now; keep both as an experiment branch (or close). Reasons: (1) lust 0.2.0 and lust next reject main + #93 on 14 of 18 targets (R222 code: osvfs.rs L0110 lust type-check gap, transport_unix.rs L0612 no AsFd in lust std), so #95's job would fail on every main push; (2) no meaningful dev-cycle gain: cargo check is 1.7% of agent Bash wait (0.50 of 30.1 h), lust can replace 17 of 87 checks, #93 saves 0 h/week today and 0.75 to 1.09 h/week after lust accepts main; lust 0.2.0 is slower than cargo check on real edits (median 8.09 vs 6.12 s), unreleased 6ced2b86 faster (1.43 s); #95 saves 0 (rules require Cargo bins; nothing consumes the artifact); (3) cost and risk: full revision, #93 weakens a protected multi_program assert, #95 job runs sticky-disk content as code with the runtime token and sudo while other branches can write that disk. Perf gap: lust tsc 1.21x cycles of our PGO+BOLT tsc (1.13x of release.yml's linux-x64); causes: out-of-line calls Cargo inlines, no BOLT (32% of gap), mimalloc, C code quality. Going harder (ThinLTO + BOLT + jemalloc) closes about 40% (to about 1.13x of ours) but the 10 s loop becomes 82 s to 13.5 min; whole-program opts blocked by lust (ThinLTO hot-copy symbol clash, full LTO undefined symbols). Side findings queued as lanes: noembed builds write a different .tsbuildinfo on effect and hono (release linux-x64 is noembed: possible product bug); testbox.yml pull_request validation job can commit the evidence target/ sticky disk (Blacksmith Branch Protection off: dashboard action for Theo); perf.sh reports cycles 0 on testboxes; release.yml linux-x64 tsc 7% slower than our full recipe (musl memcpy, no BOLT).

Load is 1.2x to 2.5x faster in Bun (new since bunperf1, cause unknown). Per-thread check caches: about 1% to 2.5%. Decision D-A for Theo: keep parked (a) or approve an opt-in shared-store mode with a second output contract (Go --singleThreaded reference, counts excluded, stability test) (b); size 10k to 20k lines. D-B to D-F: no change.
